definitions.explanation: A long, deep breath expressing sadness, tiredness, relief, or longing.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れて{溜息|ためいき}をついた。
{彼女|かのじょ}の{美|うつく}しさに{溜息|ためいき}が{出|で}た。
{深|ふか}い{溜息|ためいき}をつく。
examples.english: I let out a deep sigh.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わらなくて、{思|おも}わず{溜息|ためいき}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: The work wasn't getting done, and I involuntarily let out a sigh.

examples.japanese: {景色|けしき}があまりにも{美|うつく}しくて、{溜息|ためいき}が{出|で}るほどだった。
examples.english: The scenery was so beautiful that it was breathtaking.

notes:
{溜息|ためいき} means a sigh — a long, deep breath expressing various emotions. Often written in hiragana as ため{息|いき}.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {溜息|ためいき}をつく: to sigh (deliberate or habitual)
- {溜息|ためいき}が{出|で}る: to sigh (involuntarily)
- {深|ふか}い{溜息|ためいき}: a deep sigh
- {溜息|ためいき}まじりに: with a sigh, sigh-tinged
- {溜息|ためいき}が{出|で}るほど: so [beautiful/bad] that it makes you sigh

EMOTIONS EXPRESSED:
- Tiredness, exhaustion
- Sadness, disappointment, frustration
- Relief (after tension passes)
- Admiration, being impressed ({美|うつく}しさに{溜息|ためいき}が{出|で}る = sigh at the beauty)

CULTURAL NOTE:
There is a common saying: {溜息|ためいき}をつくと{幸|しあわ}せが{逃|に}げる (if you sigh, happiness will run away). Frequent sighing is sometimes seen as bringing bad luck or lowering the mood of those around you.
